News
NVIDIA GTC 2023 Grace Superchip With Jensen
What an odd few weeks. The big news today, of course, is that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as NVIDIA’s CEO . The markets immediately responded by adding roughly 30% or about $1T in market cap. I think folks realized this was the right option.
Jensen is BACK at NVIDIA
One of the big catalysts to this was that the U.S. government came out and said that they do not believe that having Jensen as the CEO of NVIDIA is a national security risk.
“ In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. ” ( Source : NVIDIA)
It seems the government sign-off gave the board air cover on one major risk factor: that the Megaspeed issue would turn into a major national security investigation. With that off the table, then there was the challenge of alleged workplace conduct.
NVIDIA GTC 2024 Jensen Approved Samsung HMB3E 12H
Workplace conduct is always a challenge because it opens NVIDIA up to claims from current and former employees. There was an early 2010’s case in California (note I have a 2007 JD from California’s largest law school, but never practiced, so this is not legal advice) for workplace sexual harassment in the $168M range, that was then significantly reduced to under $100M, then settled. What I have been telling folks for the past week and a half is that for the company to lose $1T in shareholder value, even $1B in a legal fund pays a lot of attorneys to cover other claims. It felt like Jensen’s value was wildly out of line with what it would cost to settle the cases. Again, I am not condoning the allegations, but at some point, I would have a hard time believing NVIDIA’s board did not have a team developing a range of exposure if they were to settle claims that could then be weighed against the cost of not having Jensen on the team. When it was comparing those two numbers plus potential government action, I can see how a board would have been more conservative.
Perhaps the other big one is that NVIDIA’s team accepted the news publicly, but what is hard to quantify is that folks who have been at NVIDIA for many years and built this enormous business are very loyal to Jensen. It has been really strange reading mainstream media reports about how Jensen can get passionate in meetings as if that were a major issue. Every CEO, especially founders, gets passionate because the business is personal. I would venture to guess that any of Jensen’s direct reports who have been there for a few years have earned enough to walk away if they wanted to, and they truly did not like working for Jensen. Maybe to put it another way, in the week and a half since Jensen resigned, I never heard an NVIDIA employee say “good riddance” or anything like that. Folks supported the board, but only spoke positively about Jensen’s leadership. It turns out when you create a market segment big enough to be measured in percentage of US GDP, it creates wealth for your employees, suppliers, customers, and partners that makes them loyal. Installing someone from the outside as CEO just does not replace that.
Final Words
More than a few executives were probably hoping to land the role and are disappointed, but realistically, those are hard shoes to fill. Jensen’s focus on the AI supply chain, sales to big customers, and loyalty among employees who have done well under his watch are exceptionally hard for anyone to replicate. Moreover, executives might be able to rise to the job, but NVIDIA added over $55B in revenue last quarter versus the year-ago quarter. Revenue-wise, that is roughly in the ballpark of adding an American Airlines annual revenue to NVIDIA on a quarterly basis. Moving that fast, it is hard for someone to grow in place in that role.
Dell DTW 2026 Keynote Day 1 Jensen
Perhaps the most fascinating part is what this means for executive compensation. The market saw what it meant to have Jensen out as NVIDIA’s CEO not just for NVIDIA, but for others in the ecosystem. Delaware’s compensation cases with Elon Musk now have a new data point showing this class of CEO can have an outsized impact on shareholder value. Not all CEOs are the same, and an individual can be uniquely valuable to an organization. Is Lisa Su the same at AMD? What about Mark Zuckerberg at Meta? Hock Tan at Broadcom? Michael Dell and Jeff Clarke? Or someone like Matt Murphy, who took Marvell from a very rough company a decade ago to a company zipping along today? The other side of this is figuring out the set of circumstances and formula for when a high-flying CEO can be ousted.
Marvell Computex 2026 Keynote Jensen
Personally, I think the board made the right decision in bringing Jensen back to NVIDIA, even if it means some clean-up needs to happen.
